keyVerseText: And he brought up Hadassah, that is, Esther, his uncle's daughter: for she had neither father nor mother, and the maid was fair and beautiful ; whom Mordecai, when her father and mother were dead, took for his own daughter. brought: Heb. nourished fair: Heb. fair of form, and good of countenance
rootMeaning: The name אֶסְתֵּר (ʼEçtêr) is of Persian derivation and literally means "star." This etymology highlights the luminous and guiding nature associated with the name, beyond its function as a proper noun. Understanding Esther as "star" adds a layer of symbolic meaning, portraying her as a shining figure in the narrative and a beacon of hope for her people.
usageInScripture: The word אֶסְתֵּר appears 55 times in the biblical text, predominantly as a proper name referring to the Jewish heroine Esther. The top translations consistently render the word simply as "Esther," with occasional contextual phrases such as "And Esther" or "So Esther," indicating its use primarily as a personal name throughout the book. This consistency underscores the centrality of Esther as a character rather than a common noun, emphasizing her unique role in the narrative.
theologicalSignificance: The name Esther, meaning "star," carries theological significance as it reflects God's providential guidance and illumination in the midst of darkness for His people. As the Jewish heroine who rises to queenship, Esther embodies the idea of God raising a light in a foreign land to preserve His covenant people. Her story reminds believers of God's sovereign hand working through individuals to fulfill His redemptive purposes, encouraging faith and courage in the face of adversity. Recognizing the meaning of her name enriches our appreciation of her role as a vessel of divine deliverance.
keyVerseReflection: Esther 2:7 introduces Esther as Hadassah, emphasizing her identity as the orphaned daughter of Abihail, whom Mordecai lovingly raised. The verse highlights her beauty and the care she received, setting the stage for her pivotal role. The name Esther, meaning "star," here points to her destined prominence and the light she would bring to her people, underscoring the providential care behind her rise to queenship.
